title: How to Install a Whole-House Water Softener | Ask This Old House (Video Analysis)

locations.name: Probable: New Jersey basement installation site (Pam's home)
locations.basis: Transcript includes explicit references to traveling to New Jersey and performing work in the basement, suggesting the install occurs in a home basement there; filming location not definitively identified.

summary: The video demonstrates diagnosing hard water, testing its mineral content, and installing a whole-house water softener with an ion-exchange resin system. It explains how resin beads remove magnesium and calcium, how brine regeneration recharges the resin, and how to plumb the unit into the cold-water supply with a drain/air-gap, bypass, and valves. The host also covers layout considerations, connections (3/8 tubing and compression fittings), maintenance (salt checks and annual refills), and the anticipated benefits—cleaner dishes and clothes, and removal of staining—while noting the system’s metered regeneration feature and safety of softened water.
topics: not dangerous to drink after softening

sections.title: Diagnosis: Hard Water Symptoms
sections.description: Richard identifies hard water as the problem, describing mineral staining and deposits, and notes that drinking the water isn’t dangerous. Patrick confirms hardness with a water reading (17 grains), establishing the need for pretreatment through a softener.

sections.title: How a Water Softener Works (Resin Beads and Brine)
sections.description: Patrick describes the softener’s two main components (resin tank and salt/brine tank) and how resin beads trap hardness minerals (magnesium/calcium) from the water, acting like a magnetic sponge, with regeneration via brine that recharges the resin.

sections.title: System Layout and Bypass Planning
sections.description: The team maps how the cold-water supply enters the house, where the softener should be placed, and how the bypass keeps the unit serviceable: water routes through the softener when bypass is closed, and a bypass path allows taking the unit offline for maintenance.

sections.title: Connections: Tubing, Drain, and Air Gap
sections.description: The video shows making connections: 3/8" plastic tubing with compression fittings to the softener and brine tank, routing a drain line to the sewer, and using an air-gap to prevent potable water contact with sewage.

sections.title: Operation, Placement, and Maintenance Considerations
concepts: unit placement relative to floor and water meter
sections.description: The host highlights the smart feature: a built-in water meter that triggers regeneration only when water is used, explains salt-top maintenance (check salt monthly, refill ~twice a year), and notes the final benefits of softened water for laundry, dishes, and reducing stains.

featured_techniques.technique: Ion-exchange resin beads attract calcium and magnesium from water (hardness removal)
Brine regeneration recharges resin by passing salt solution through it
Air-gap drain connection to prevent contamination between potable water and sewage
Meter-based regeneration control inside the softener
Bypass valve configuration allows service without shutting off main supply
Soldering copper pipe and installing 3/8 inch tubing with compression fittings
